topics.label: Lecture Introduction and the Hallmarks of Cancer Framework
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning outcomes, previous lecture context, and the Hallmarks of Cancer framework used to study tumor progression.

topics.label: Growth Signal Autonomy and Proliferative Signaling Cascades
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in signaling pathways such as Wnt, receptor tyrosine kinases, and TGF-beta drive cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Leukemias and Epithelial Cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells fail to undergo terminal differentiation and remain trapped in proliferative states across hematopoietic lineages and intestinal crypts.

topics.label: Evasion of Apoptosis and Mitochondrial Permeabilization
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how tumor cells resist programmed cell death through alterations in p53, Bax, and Bcl-2 signaling.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality, Telomere Maintenance, and Senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit and senescence via telomerase activation while contrasting this with normal p53-mediated stress responses.

topics.label: Altered Cancer Metabolism and Epigenetic Feedback
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics transition to complex hallmarks and explain how tumor cells rewire cellular metabolism through aerobic glycolysis and oncometabolite-driven epigenetic modifications.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis and Neovascularization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the necessity, timing, and molecular balance of angiogenic signaling required to sustain tumor growth.

topics.label: The Metastatic Cascade and Clonal Evolution in Secondary Sites
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the biological stages, physical and environmental barriers, diagnostics, and genomic features underlying cancer metastasis.

topics.label: Closing Summary and Practical Information
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a recap of cancer hallmarks, references to further reading, and practical announcements.
